reason: Conversation 2 handled the opener well: it asked whether H98 was a display code or part of the model, then explained that H98 means a microwave power circuit fault (inverter or magnetron). It used the grill working as a diagnostic clue, suggested one power reset and the water test, avoided claiming it was definitely one part, and told the user plainly to get an engineer and agree a fixed quote, giving practical repair-versus-replace thresholds and cover checks. Conversation 1 ignored the user's repeated answers and the model number, kept asking about inverters after being told the user did not know what one was, gave only generic cost advice, and ended by asking about low power or grill mode, which the user had already effectively answered. It never clearly recommended an engineer visit or offered a useful next step, so it served the homeowner much worse.
